findings.evidence: Lines 570-654: the `Lp` section cites only `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_le` (lines 580, 652); grep shows no use of `maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup` or `mul_measure_lt_maximalFunction_le` after line 566.

findings.issue: Rewritten docstring says "Together with `TauCeti.maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup` (the case `p = ∞`) and `TauCeti.mul_measure_lt_maximalFunction_le` (the weak-type substitute at `p = 1`), this supplies the estimate used below to define ... `maximalFunctionLp`." findings.evidence: Line 621-622: `def maximalFunctionLp (μ : Measure E) ... (p : ℝ≥0∞) (hp : 1 < p) (hp_top : p ≠ ∞)`; compare line 607-608 "in `Lᵖ`, for `1 < p < ∞`".
findings.fix: Say "for `1 < p < ∞`" in the first sentence, as `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal` and `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top` already do.
findings.issue: `maximalFunctionLp`'s docstring — "The Hardy–Littlewood maximal function as a well-defined nonlinear map on `Lᵖ`" — never states that the definition exists only for `1 < p < ∞`, even though the definition takes `hp : 1 < p` and `hp_top : p ≠ ∞` as arguments and all its supporting lemmas are restricted to that range.

findings.evidence: Lines 99-102 vs. lines 97-98, which state "for `1 < p < ∞`" for the strong-type bullet; all three cited declarations (lines 583, 609, 621) hypothesise `1 < p` and `p ≠ ∞`.
findings.fix: Add the range: "for `1 < p < ∞`, the maximal function of an `Lᵖ` function is finite almost everywhere; ...".
findings.issue: Same omission in the new module-docstring bullet: "the maximal function is finite almost everywhere on `Lᵖ`; its real-valued representative preserves `MemLp` and descends to a nonlinear map `Lp F p μ → Lp ℝ p μ`" — read against the preceding bullets (which do qualify "for `1 < p < ∞`") this promises an unrestricted-`p` statement the file does not prove.

summary: Every new declaration carries a docstring, but the edited docstring on `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_le` now makes a false joint claim about the endpoint lemmas, and the headline new definition plus its module-docstring bullet drop the `1 < p < ∞` restriction they actually require.
